about: Hand-authored classification ledger. scripts/docs/classify.ps1 merges it into the inventory produced by scripts/docs/inventory.ps1 and fails when a document has no entry, when an entry names a document that no longer exists, when a live document under docs/ is missing from docs/README.md, or when a canonical document holds an actionable backlog. Deciding what a document IS remains a judgement: it is written here so a reviewer can disagree with a line, not buried in a regex. Most documents are covered by a directory rule; a document earns its own entry only when it is an exception.
updated: 2026-08-13 (docs reorganised by function; the second backlog removed and replaced by GitHub Issues)

proposed_type.canon: Design truth about a system or about the product. Lives in exactly one document.
proposed_type.guideline: How to do something: pipeline, conventions, patterns, design language.
proposed_type.spec: Implementation-facing description of what the code does.
proposed_type.process: How the team and its agents work.
proposed_type.routing: Decides who works and what they read. Not a design source.
proposed_type.record: Dated history, read-only after the fact.
proposed_type.generated: Produced by a script. Never hand-edited.
proposed_type.index: Table of contents for a directory.

authority.derived: Must follow a canonical document; loses on conflict.
authority.historical: Describes a past state. Never wins over the present.
authority.generated: Measurement. Wins over prose about the same numbers.

action.keep: Stays where it is, as it is.
action.merge: Should be folded into another document.
action.split: Mixes two types and should be divided.

rules.note: One document per game system: what it is, the problem it solves for the player, its authority in code, its invariants, how it manifests, who consumes it. No sequencing and no future work.
Product-level canon: the fantasy, the pillars, the guardrails, and the eight lineages.
Design language and asset pipeline. A guideline may say 'use X for Y'; it may not say 'implement X later'.
Upstream license text and LPC credit data. A distribution obligation, not documentation.
Machine-readable manifest for the 16 imported lineage character scenes.
The code's own contracts: layers and their enforcement, state ownership, conventions, verification, performance budgets, review guide.
Routing layer. Decides which agent and which skills handle a request. Never a design source.
Decision records, kept only where a current rule is counterintuitive and the reason is not visible in the code.
Written by tools/New-SessionSnapshot.ps1. The measured baseline plus a dated frame. Never hand-edited.
Canonical skills and agent definitions. Mirrors under .claude/ and .codex/ are generated from these.
Generated mirror. Never hand-edit; run scripts/Sync-AgentContext.ps1.
Generated mirror. Never hand-edit; run scripts/Sync-AgentContext.ps1.

README.md.note: Public face of the repository. Points at the docs index and at GitHub Issues; carries no status of its own.

AGENTS.md.note: Shares its source of truth with CLAUDE.md by design: same hard rules, different runtime. The duplication is deliberate and must stay synchronised by hand.

CHANGELOG.md.note: One entry per increment: what a player can now do that they could not before, and the schema range crossed. Exempt from the backlog guard because history legitimately describes work that was once pending.

docs/README.md.note: The documentation index and the authority rules. Completeness is enforced: classify.ps1 fails when a live document under docs/ is not listed here.

docs/engineering/visual-regression.md.note: Two jobs in one file, deliberately: the required fixture matrix and sign-off checklist are a contract, and the dated review record below them is history. The record is what makes a signature meaningful, so it stays beside the checklist rather than in docs/history/.

docs/ai/FEATURE_HANDOFF_TEMPLATE.md.note: A form, not a queue. Its unchecked boxes are the blanks a person fills in per handoff; they name no work the repository owes.

docs/session-state/README.md.note: Explains why the directory exists and why STATE.txt must never be hand-edited. The only non-generated file under session-state/.
